# Behaviour question sheet — `language-vocab`

**3 decisions · 12 reviews.** Generated by `node kit.js sheet language-vocab --rev language-vocab@8228db7`, over the app at `language-vocab@8228db7`. Do not hand-edit — re-run it.

## What this is

Kit read this app's `docs/DESIGN.md` and its backend test names and built one list of
behaviours from both. Everything it read out of the **code** is marked unreviewed until a
human rules on it, because an inference that quietly becomes a specification is the failure
this whole thing exists to prevent.

The two sections below are not the same job and should not take the same effort:

- **Decisions** — Kit can prove both answers change something: either nothing documented
  displays this surface, or two behaviours contradict each other about one value. Each one
  carries the evidence, the options, my recommendation, and the strongest case against it.
- **Reviews** — the code asserts this, a documented screen needs it, and it looks right.
  One line each. If one is wrong, it becomes a decision.

## Decisions — 3

### D1. DESIGN.md defers other languages but promises the data model is language-tagged from day one. It got more than a column: `language` is a required parameter on all three IPoolService methods, so every drill route in PR 4 has to carry it too. Is language a PARAMETER, or a setting the app is configured with?

**`BEH-LANG-1` — Every pool operation is scoped to one language**

**Why this is a decision:** you said the API layer is inferred from what the UI needs to
display. This surface exists in the code and **no documented screen displays it**, so either
the design is missing a screen or the surface should go. Those are opposite edits.

**Evidence** — read out of `backend/Balenthiran.LanguageVocab.Tests/PoolServiceTests.cs:Bootstrap_only_touches_the_requested_language`:

- bootstrap for one language leaves another language's pool untouched
- the loader throws when the language is missing

**Options**

- **Keep it threaded** — IPoolService.cs:17,24,31 keep `string language`, and the drill routes take it as a path segment or query param. The isolation property stays enforced. Adding Cantonese is then a seed file and a config value, with no signature to change and no migration. Cost: every route, client call and test in PR 4 carries an argument whose only possible value today is `zh`.
- **Make it ambient** — Drop the parameter; one configured language, resolved from settings or an owner record. VocabItemEntity.cs:14 already defaults Language to \"zh\", so the column and the seed loader's per-language files survive untouched — the roadmap promise DESIGN.md actually makes is kept. The isolation test loses its subject, and language 2 becomes a signature change across the service, the routes and the client.

**I'd pick: Keep it threaded.** The parameter is not speculative surface — it is the roadmap promise DESIGN.md:36-37 states, made executable. And the moment to pay for it is now, before PR 4 exists: threading it through routes that are not written yet costs one argument each, where retrofitting it later means changing a shipped API and regenerating a client. A6-style single-user apps are also where an ambient global is hardest to unpick, because the assumption gets read into a dozen call sites first.

**The strongest case against that:** The isolation test seeds a synthetic \"fr\" that exists nowhere else in the repo — 150 HSK1 entries in one file, one language, zero users asking for a second. So a required argument is being carried on every method and every future route to satisfy a property no caller can exercise, and the test proves the code does what it was written to do rather than anything about the product. \"Other languages\" is under **Explicitly deferred**, and a deferred feature that still shapes today's signatures has not really been deferred. The cheap version is to keep the Language COLUMN — which is all DESIGN.md literally promises — and let the parameter arrive with the second language, when its shape will be known rather than guessed.

**Your answer** — becomes: `serves BEH-…` added to `BEH-LANG-1` (with the screen written into `DESIGN.md`), or `BEH-LANG-1` deleted along with the surface it describes.

### D2. The string `Sentence` occurs exactly twice in this repo: the enum member, and the DESIGN.md line reserving it. No seed entry sets a type, no route exposes one, the frontend has no such field. Does the reservation stay, or does the type arrive with sentence mode?

**`BEH-ITEMTYPE-1` — A vocabulary item has a type, defaulting to word**

**Why this is a decision:** you said the API layer is inferred from what the UI needs to
display. This surface exists in the code and **no documented screen displays it**, so either
the design is missing a screen or the surface should go. Those are opposite edits.

**Evidence** — read out of `backend/Balenthiran.LanguageVocab.Tests/SeedLoaderTests.cs:Load_defaults_item_type_to_word`:

- the schema reserves a Sentence type that nothing produces or consumes

**Options**

- **Keep the reservation** — VocabItemType.cs keeps `Sentence = 1`. It pins `Word = 0` as the default, so the enum can be extended later without renumbering a persisted column, and it makes DESIGN.md:34-35's second phase legible in the code a reader actually opens.
- **Drop it until it is built** — The enum becomes `Word = 0` alone. Adding a member back later is one line and no migration, since nothing has ever persisted a 1. The type column, the nullable SeedEntry.Type and the defaulting test all survive — only the unreachable value goes.

**I'd pick: Keep the reservation.** This is the cheapest kind of reserved surface there is: an enum member costs no route, no client field, no migration and no test, and it is the one place a persisted integer genuinely benefits from being fixed early — `Word = 0` is only guaranteed if nothing renumbers around it. It is also already documented, which is the distinction this corpus is built to draw: reserved-and-written-down is not the same as surface nobody asked for.

**The strongest case against that:** You have one other behaviour in this corpus (BEH-LANG-1) making the same bet on the same deferred roadmap, and answering both the same way is how a v1 quietly acquires a v2's shape. `Word = 0` is the C# default for any enum whether or not a second member exists, so the renumbering argument protects against a hazard that only appears once someone adds a value — at which point they can append it. And a reserved member is not free in the way it looks: it is a branch every future `switch` has to handle or deliberately ignore, on a code path nothing can currently reach.

**Your answer** — becomes: `serves BEH-…` added to `BEH-ITEMTYPE-1` (with the screen written into `DESIGN.md`), or `BEH-ITEMTYPE-1` deleted along with the surface it describes.

### D3. SelectNextAsync takes a required `int seed` and NOTHING calls it outside the tests — the drill API is PR 4 and does not exist. So where the seed comes from in production has never been decided, and it is a user-visible choice, not an implementation detail. Which is it: the client sends a seed, or the server makes one?

**`BEH-DETERMINISM-1` — Selection is deterministic for a given seed**

**Why this is a decision:** you said the API layer is inferred from what the UI needs to
display. This surface exists in the code and **no documented screen displays it**, so either
the design is missing a screen or the surface should go. Those are opposite edits.

**Evidence** — read out of `backend/Balenthiran.LanguageVocab.Tests/PoolServiceTests.cs:SelectNext_is_deterministic_for_the_same_seed`:

- the same seed picks the same word, so the sampler is testable

**Options**

- **The server generates it per request** — The drill route makes a fresh seed each call. Determinism reverts to what DESIGN.md:66-67 says it is for — unit-testability — and every draw is independent. A refresh gives a different card. Resuming a session mid-way is then a separate feature with its own state, not something the seed gives you.
- **The client supplies it per session** — The frontend mints a seed when a drill starts and sends it with each draw. The same session replays the same sequence, so a refresh or a reconnect resumes where it was rather than reshuffling. It also makes the sequence reproducible from a bug report. Cost: the seed is now part of the public API contract, and a client that reuses one gets the same word forever.

**I'd pick: The server generates it per request.** DESIGN.md:66-67 says the determinism exists so the sampler is unit-testable, and that is a claim about the test suite, not a promise to a user. A4 says the picker samples weakness-weighted from the active pool — that is a property of the WEIGHTS, and it holds either way, so the seed is buying nothing the design asks for. Keeping it server-side also keeps the failure mode small: a client that mishandles a seed can pin itself to one word, and that bug is invisible until someone notices they keep seeing 好.

**The strongest case against that:** You are deciding this now, in a corpus, for a route that will be written in PR 4 — and the version that is harder to add later is the one being rejected. Making the seed part of the request from day one costs one optional query parameter and no state; retrofitting it means changing a shipped drill endpoint and regenerating the client. Resume-after-refresh on a phone is also not an exotic want for a drill app, and the pinned-to-one-word failure is preventable by advancing the seed per draw rather than by hiding it. There is a third answer this question does not offer: derive the seed from something stable you already have — user plus date — which gives a reproducible day without either a client contract or a decision about session state.

**Your answer** — becomes: `serves BEH-…` added to `BEH-DETERMINISM-1` (with the screen written into `DESIGN.md`), or `BEH-DETERMINISM-1` deleted along with the surface it describes.

## What Kit is NOT asking you here

Worth stating, because a sheet that omits its own scope reads as complete:

- **The behaviours this app has documented but not built.** Kit refuses to generate a test for a
  screen that does not exist and names the missing noun instead. That list is a build backlog,
  not a question — it goes to zero on its own as the frontend lands.
- **Anything read out of a document you wrote.** A defined behaviour is not up for adjudication
  here; you already ruled on it by writing it down. It only reappears if it collides with
  another defined behaviour — which is exactly what D1 is.
